results.title: ENT-1569: Fix model-cache FileLock stampede on cold weight download
results.text:
# ENT-1569: Fix model-cache FileLock stampede on cold weight download

- State: closed
- Author: rvirani1
- Created: 2026-08-03T21:39:03Z
- Updated: 2026-08-05T16:59:42Z
- Repository: roboflow/inference
- Number: #2752
- +1077 -295 in 7 files
- Merge commit: ddfb591cbfa01aeb04e70f3ef47c728ca3e54e07
- Reviewers: hansent, yeldarby, dkosowski87, probicheaux, PawelPeczek-Roboflow, grzegorz-roboflow, rafel-roboflow

## Labels

- claude-review

---

## Description

Linear: ENT-1569

When several pipelines on one device share a model, each has its own `ModelManager`, so per-manager `add_model` de-dupe does not help: all of them independently try to download the same weights into the shared model cache and serialize on a single per-model `FileLock`. On a cold cache the download can take longer than the lock wait window (observed 135s against the hard-coded 120s timeout), so the waiting pipelines gave up and hard-errored with `filelock.Timeout` instead of loading from the by-then warm cache. This is the recurring "lock error" reported on multi-camera edge deployments.

Note this is complementary to the workflow model pre-loading shipped in v1.3.8 (#2737): pre-loading moves the cold download to startup, but all sibling processes still race on the same lock there, so the stampede fix is needed either way.

### Changes

- Replace the hard-coded 120s download-lock timeout with `MODEL_WEIGHTS_DOWNLOAD_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 600s), giving a cold download comfortable headroom.
- Add `acquire_model_download_lock()`, which retries acquisition up to `MODEL_WEIGHTS_DOWNLOAD_LOCK_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 3) instead of letting `filelock.Timeout` propagate and kill the pipeline.
- Re-check the artifact cache after acquiring the lock, so a waiter whose sibling already completed the download skips the redundant fetch.
- Centralize the lock path in `get_model_download_lock_path()` and route all five download implementations through it (base Roboflow API paths plus SAM3-3D, transformers, and OWLv2, which carried their own copies of the hard-coded 120s lock and would otherwise have silently missed the new behavior).
- Stop unlinking the lock file in the transformers and OWLv2 paths: POSIX locks guard inodes, not path strings, so removing the file let a newly arriving process create a fresh inode at the same path and download concurrently with a waiter still blocked on the old one.
- Guard against `basename()` returning `""` for a cache dir with a trailing separator, which would have collapsed every model onto a shared `.lock`.

The lock file name intentionally stays on the historical `_file_locks/.lock` scheme: `FileLock` only coordinates processes opening the identical pathname, so renaming it would break mutual exclusion against already-deployed versions during a rolling deploy. The resulting cross-model key collisions and the existence-only cache predicate are documented inline as accepted trade-offs.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested?

- New unit tests in `tests/inference/unit_tests/core/models/test_roboflow.py`: threaded tests over the real `FileLock` plus tests driving the production download method, covering serialization, warm-cache reuse by the waiter, retry-after-timeout, and lock release on the failure path.
- `python -m pytest tests/inference/unit_tests/core/models/test_roboflow.py` — 33 passed.
- Rebased onto current `main` (post-v1.3.8); only conflict was a test-file import merge.

## Any specific deployment considerations

Two new env vars, both with safe defaults: `MODEL_WEIGHTS_DOWNLOAD_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (600) and `MODEL_WEIGHTS_DOWNLOAD_LOCK_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3). No migration; lock file naming unchanged, so mixed-version fleets keep mutual exclusion during rollout.

results.title: Synchronous model loads run inside the shared workflows thread pool, stalling all concurrent workflow runs (latency collapse with idle GPU/CPU)
results.text:
# Synchronous model loads run inside the shared workflows thread pool, stalling all concurrent workflow runs (latency collapse with idle GPU/CPU)

- State: open
- Author: imbgar-roboflow
- Created: 2026-06-11T22:38:59Z
- Updated: 2026-08-20T12:45:20Z
- Repository: roboflow/inference
- Number: #2448

---

## Summary

On a GPU inference server (`roboflow-inference-server-gpu`, build of 2026-06-05 / v1.3.0 era) serving multi-model Workflows under sustained production traffic, we observed a latency collapse mode where **p50 latency of all workflow endpoints rises 3–10x while accelerator duty cycle stays ≤13% and CPU stays under 25% of limit**. Raw `/infer/*` endpoints on the same pods remain fast. Root cause analysis points at a structural issue: **synchronous model loads (3–19s each) execute inside the shared workflows `ThreadPoolExecutor`, starving step execution for every concurrent workflow run in the process.**

## Environment

- `gpu_http:app` via uvicorn, 1 worker, defaults: `HTTP_API_SHARED_WORKFLOWS_THREAD_POOL_ENABLED=True` (16 workers), `WORKFLOWS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STEPS=4`, `MAX_ACTIVE_MODELS=20`, `MEMORY_FREE_THRESHOLD=0.20`
- Workload: ~6 workflow variants chaining 3–5 models each; working set ~12 model/version combos (~600MB VRAM each) on NVIDIA L4
- Horizontal autoscaling on request rate; replica churn redistributes traffic across pods regularly

## Observed

- `Model loaded: ... load_time=` events: p50 ≈ 5s, p90 ≈ 11s, occurring continuously in steady state (~200–700/hr fleet-wide) because the model working set + `MEMORY_FREE_THRESHOLD` VRAM guard keeps the `WithFixedSizeCache` manager evicting (`reason=memory_pressure`) and re-loading
- When autoscaler churn raises per-pod cache-miss rates, workflow p50/p90 explodes (0.8s → 4–8s p90 across **all** workflow endpoints uniformly) while GPU duty cycle ≤13% and CPU well under limit — classic heavy-tailed-service queueing on a software bottleneck (E[S²] dominated by inline loads), not a hardware one
- `/infer/*` on the same pods degrades only mildly (~2x p90 at worst) — consistent with it not using the shared workflows pool, only the model-manager lock

## Code path

- `inference/core/interfaces/http/http_api.py` (~L1193): one process-global `self.shared_thread_pool_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16)` is created and passed to every `ExecutionEngine.init(...)` (~L1293)
- Model blocks execute as steps in that pool; a cold model triggers `add_model` → download + deserialize + VRAM upload (3–19s) **inside a step worker**, while also holding the `WithFixedSizeCache` queue lock for eviction bookkeeping (`inference/core/managers/decorators/fixed_size_cache.py`), so concurrent runs both lose a pool worker and contend on the lock
- Under churn, several in-flight loads consume a large fraction of the 16 workers; queued steps back up; every workflow run slows; in-flight requests then pile up to whatever the ASGI concurrency limit is, producing 503 load shedding while the GPU is idle

## Asks

1. **Isolate model loading from step execution** — run loads on a dedicated loader executor (or async path) so a cold model only blocks requests that need that model, never the shared step pool
2. **First-class model pre-warming**: a way to declare the deployment's model set to be loaded at startup (and pinned), with readiness gated on warm-up, so steady-state inline loads approach zero (the `_pinned_models` machinery in `WithFixedSizeCache` looks close but isn't exposed/documented for this)
3. **Hysteresis / actively-used protection on `memory_pressure` evictions** — under the VRAM threshold, LRU eviction of models that are in active rotation creates a permanent evict↔reload cycle
4. **Observability**: counters/histograms for model load duration, cache miss rate, and shared-pool queue depth would have made this diagnosable from metrics instead of log archaeology

Happy to provide more detail on the analysis.

## Timeline

**imbgar-roboflow** commented on 2026-06-11T22:54:01Z:

> Additional finding on **why** eviction churn was chronic in this setup: `memory_pressure_detected()` (fixed_size_cache.py:283) only calls `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` and re-checks free memory **when `USE_INFERENCE_MODELS=True`**. With `USE_INFERENCE_MODELS=False` (our config), `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` counts the torch caching allocator's reclaimable blocks as used — so a pod whose actual model working set was ~7GB on a 24GB L4 still read <20% free and cycled evict↔reload continuously (200–700 loads/hr fleet-wide). Suggest calling `empty_cache()` (or consulting `torch.cuda.memory_reserved() - memory_allocated()`) before the eviction decision regardless of `USE_INFERENCE_MODELS`, since fragmentation/cached blocks otherwise masquerade as memory pressure.

**imbgar-roboflow** commented on 2026-06-11T23:17:00Z:

> Correction to my previous comment after pulling actual GPU memory telemetry: the eviction pressure in our case was **real, not a misread**. `kubernetes_io:container_accelerator_memory_used` shows 18.3–20.0GB used on the 24GB card throughout — the deployment's model working set (~15 model/version combos; per-model `vram_bytes` from unload logs ranging 0.6–13.5GB) genuinely cannot co-reside, so the evict↔reload cycle is structural oversubscription, not allocator-cache misattribution. The `empty_cache` gating note stands as a design observation, but per-backend it also wouldn't have helped here (legacy mode VRAM is largely ONNX Runtime arena-held, which `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` can't release).\n\nThis strengthens asks 1 and 2 though: when a working set is larger than VRAM, steady-state inline loads are *guaranteed*, so isolating loads from the shared step pool and supporting working-set-aware admission/pinning is what separates 'slower tail' from 'whole-pod stalls'.

**voropaevv** commented on 2026-08-20T12:45:20Z:

> ## Current-main reproduction
> 
> On current `main` (`262fba8286ef6048f11f953b3a87808555f4f0d2`), I reproduced
> the starvation using explicit synchronization in both a local model of the
> synchronous HTTP/shared-executor topology and the real
> `run_steps_in_parallel()` helper. With all shared workers in cold loads, a
> simulated warm request starts but its step waits for a worker. This is not yet
> a full ASGI reproduction; that remains a production acceptance test.
> 
> ## Incomplete isolation options
> 
> The local comparison also showed that:
> 
> - a loader executor still starves the shared pool if its worker waits on
> `future.result()`;
> - #2737 preloading moves static and `$inputs.*` loads, but synchronous waiting
> can instead saturate AnyIO request capacity;
> - an unlocked `model_id in manager` check loses the reproduced
> readiness-to-eviction race in `WithFixedSizeCache(ModelManager(...))`;
> - `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N)` bounds workers, not queued submissions;
> - typed deferral releases the shared worker and lets unrelated warm work start
> while physical loading proceeds elsewhere.
>

# v1.3.7

- Tag: v1.3.7
- Repository: roboflow/inference
- Published: 2026-07-27T17:07:23Z
- Author: PawelPeczek-Roboflow

---

# 🚀 Added 
 
## ✈️ `OFFLINE_MODE` — air-gapped deployments 
 
Inference servers can now run fully air-gapped (@alexnorell, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2263). The supported flow is deliberately simple: 
1. **Warm** a mounted cache while network access and a Roboflow API key are available. 
2. **Restart** the same deployment with the same cache, `OFFLINE_MODE=True`, and no API key. 
3. Cached model metadata, weights, and Workflow specifications load with no built-in Roboflow API calls, no retries, and no cache-expiration failures. 
 
## 📏 YOLO26 depth estimation 
 
Public-pretrained **YOLO26 depth estimation** lands end-to-end as a drop-in alternative to Depth Anything (@leeclemnet, 
https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2691): `inference_models` backends for **ONNX, TorchScript, and TensorRT** (Ultralytics `-depth` pretrains, 768×768, metric log-depth head), public aliases `yolo26{n,s,m,l,x}-depth-768`, and the same five variants selectable in the `roboflow_core/depth_estimation@v1` Workflow block. Outputs are normalized to Depth Anything's disparity-style convention (larger = closer), so downstream tooling is interchangeable; the block's default model is unchanged. 
 
Alongside it, **depth maps got dramatically cheaper on the wire** (@leeclemnet, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2693): the SDK now requests the normalized depth map as a **base64 PNG16** (uint16 quantization of the normalized map) instead of a JSON list of floats — roughly **17 MB → ~1 MB** for a typical single-image response, with matching decode-time wins. 
Raw HTTP callers are unaffected (the server-side default response format is still `json`), and the SDK decoder transparently accepts responses from older servers. 
 
## 🔥 New workflow blocks 
 
- **Detections Nearest Neighbor** (`roboflow_core/detections_nearest_neighbor@v1`) — a nearest-neighbor spatial join between two detection sets: for each query detection it finds the closest target detection(s) by 2D pixel distance between configurable anchor points (bbox corners/edges/center, or a named keypoint), with tie-awareness, self-match exclusion, and an optional `max_distance` cutoff (@bczifra, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2698). Emits enriched query predictions (`nearest_target_distance`) plus index-aligned matched-query/matched-target sets ready for standard downstream blocks. 
- **Grid Visualization** now accepts **multiple image inputs** directly (@leeclemnet, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2694). 
 
## 🎛️ Execution & operations 
 
- **Per-run workflow sink disabling** — a `disable_sinks` API parameter, delivered to sink blocks through the existing dependency-injection system, turns off built-in sink side effects for a single run while the rest of the workflow executes normally; all 22 built-in side-effect sinks honor it with no manifest or spec changes (@joaomarcoscrs, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2697). 
- **TensorRT engine builds announce themselves** — with the TRT execution provider and a cold engine cache, the first inference silently compiles an engine (measured ~9.5 minutes for a single COCO object-detection model on an Orin 16 GB) while requests time out. The server now logs an explicit warning at session-configuration time, pointing at the mitigation: persist `MODEL_CACHE_DIR` (@sberan, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2703). 
- **Billable and errored usage are aggregated separately** — usage records now partition by billability, request outcome, structured `error_type`, and bounded HTTP `error_status_code` (400–599), so a failed request can no longer blend into a billable aggregate; billing *intent* is preserved and policy stays with the Roboflow backend. Payload schema is additive-only (@hansent, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2692). 
- **Roboflow API calls now default to a 120-second timeout** (`ROBOFLOW_API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`) instead of waiting indefinitely (@sberan, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2702). 
 
# 🔧 Fixed 
 
- **Instance-segmentation dense-mask post-processing memory bounded** — mask upscaling now runs in fixed-size chunks and RF-DETR segmentation applies the standard `max_detections` cap (default 300, overridable via `INFERENCE_MODELS_RFDETR_DEFAULT_MAX_DETECTIONS`) *before* the expensive full-resolution work. Peak CUDA memory on a dense-instance workload dropped **17.1 GiB → 4.2 GiB** with no wall-time regression (@bigbitbus, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2682). 
- **Model-access failures keep their real HTTP statuses** — Execution Engine v1.12.1 propagates upstream model-access errors (401/402/403/404…) through workflow runs instead of collapsing them into generic 500s (@hansent, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2690; @dkosowski87, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2709). 
- **PP-OCR** — authorization fixed on Serverless (@Erol444, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2646), and the route now returns a clean 404 when the `inference_models` stack is disabled instead of an internal error (@dkosowski87, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2707). 
- **Phantom keypoints eliminated** — padded keypoint slots are no longer emitted as real keypoints in predictions (@kounelisagis, 
 https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2677). 
- **`detections_overlaps` kind round-trips** — serializer and deserializer registered, so the kind survives workflow JSON output/input (@kounelisagis, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2638). 
- **Grounding DINO accepts both canonical and legacy BERT cache layouts**, so existing warmed caches keep working after the cache-layout changes (@dkosowski87, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2716). 
- **SAM3 package load no longer requires `sam_configuration.json`** (@grzegorz-roboflow, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2678). 
- **Local package imports no longer write `.pyc` bytecode during module execution**, keeping mounted/read-only caches byte-stable (@dkosowski87, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2713). 
- **Pre-release security patches** — landing-page npm dependency chain moved to patched versions and Python dependency bumps rolled up ahead of the release (@PawelPeczek-Roboflow, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2715). 
 
# 🚧 Maintenance 
 
- **`inference-models` 0.33.0 / 0.34.1 releases and pins** (@PawelPeczek-Roboflow, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2706; @dkosowski87, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2711). 
- **Windows build fixes** (@PawelPeczek-Roboflow, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2689). 
- **CI** — PP-OCR T4 regression tests skipped when `USE_INFERENCE_MODELS=False` (@grzegorz-roboflow, https://github.com/roboflow/inference/pull/2712) and the workflows integration-test job timeout raised to 25 minutes (@grzegorz-roboflow, https://

# [codex] Fix request metadata tracking for nested model-manager decorators

- State: merged
- Author: hansent
- Created: 2026-04-02T22:03:26Z
- Updated: 2026-04-03T11:02:01Z
- Repository: roboflow/inference
- Number: #2198
- +38 -0 in 2 files
- Merged: 2026-04-03T11:01:59Z
- Merge commit: 70e2c4a034dd0432729ef62016fbc6a23022f379
- Reviewers: yeldarby, dkosowski87, probicheaux, grzegorz-roboflow

---

## Summary

Fixes a regression introduced in #2183 where warm-model requests can fail with `500 Internal Server Error` in the parallel server path.

The failure showed up in the integration build here:
- GitHub Actions run 23904399202 / job 69709194003

## Problem

After #2183 added request metadata tracking for loaded models, parallel-server integration tests started failing across multiple inference routes with 500s.

Although the surface symptom looked like a route-level regression, the actual failure was happening deeper in the model-manager decorator stack during warm-model handling.

## Root Cause

The new request-metadata tracking added calls to `record_request_metadata()` from warm-model paths in the cache/decorator layer.

That works when the wrapped object is a plain `ModelManager`, but the parallel server uses a nested decorator stack:

`WithFixedSizeCache(LockedLoadModelManagerDecorator(ModelManager))`

In that configuration, the warm-path metadata call could land on `LockedLoadModelManagerDecorator`, which inherits from `ModelManagerDecorator` but does not own the `_model_request_aliases` / `_model_request_paths` state introduced in #2183.

That caused the failure seen in CI:

`AttributeError: 'LockedLoadModelManagerDecorator' object has no attribute '_model_request_aliases'`

So the bug was not that request metadata was conceptually wrong; it was that nested decorators were not forwarding metadata writes to the underlying base manager that actually owns the tracking state.

## What Changed

- Added `ModelManagerDecorator.record_request_metadata()` so metadata writes are forwarded to the wrapped manager.
- Added a regression test covering the nested decorator stack used by the parallel server:
 - `WithFixedSizeCache(LockedLoadModelManagerDecorator(ModelManager))`

## Impact

- Fixes warm-request failures in the parallel server path.
- Preserves the request metadata tracking added in #2183.
- Ensures nested decorators behave correctly when request metadata is recorded for already-loaded models.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/inference/unit_tests/core/managers/test_base.py tests/inference/unit_tests/core/managers/test_decorators.py`

## Notes

This is a focused follow-up to #2183: it keeps the new metadata behavior, but fixes the decorator forwarding bug exposed by the integration run above.

# docs/workflows/benchmarks.md

- Branch: main
- Repository: roboflow/inference

---

# Workflows Benchmarks

This page compares **direct** model inference latency versus **Workflow-wrapped inference** latency for popular detection models. The goal is to quantify the overhead introduced by the Workflows execution engine.

## Self-Hosted Results

All times are in **milliseconds**. Benchmarks were run on a server-grade NVIDIA GPU using TensorRT-optimized models, called directly via the `inference` Python package. Each model was warmed up before timing, then measured over 10 iterations.

| Model | Avg Direct (ms) | Avg Workflow (ms) | Workflow Overhead (ms) |
|-------|-----------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| rfdetr-nano | 2.65 | 4.40 | 1.75 |
| rfdetr-small | 3.17 | 4.62 | 1.45 |
| rfdetr-medium | 3.79 | 5.38 | 1.59 |
| rfdetr-large | 4.87 | 7.46 | 2.59 |
| rfdetr-xlarge | 8.44 | 10.65 | 2.21 |
| yolo26n-640 | 2.42 | 4.07 | 1.65 |
| yolo26s-640 | 3.25 | 5.48 | 2.23 |
| yolo26m-640 | 4.56 | 6.29 | 1.73 |
| yolo26l-640 | 5.76 | 8.01 | 2.25 |
| yolo26x-640 | 7.75 | 9.36 | 1.61 |

### Key Takeaways

- **Workflow overhead is minimal** — typically 1.5–2.6 ms on top of direct inference, regardless of model size.
- For larger models (e.g. `rfdetr-xlarge`), the workflow overhead is small relative to model inference time (~26%).
- For smaller, faster models (e.g. `yolo26n-640`), the overhead is proportionally larger but still under 2 ms in absolute terms.
- Workflow overhead is CPU-bound (graph scheduling, input preparation, output routing), while model inference itself typically runs on the GPU (when available). As a result, the overhead stays relatively constant regardless of GPU speed.

### Methodology

- GPU-accelerated inference (results will vary by hardware).
- Warmup: Each model and workflow engine is warmed up with one inference call before timing begins.
- Iterations: 10 timed iterations per method, per model.
- Direct inference: Uses `get_model()` and calls `model.infer()` directly.
- Workflow inference: Wraps the same model in a minimal single-step workflow and runs it through the Execution Engine.

??? note "Click to expand benchmark script"

    ```python
    import os
    import statistics
    import time
    import argparse
    import csv
    import requests
    import numpy as np
    from PIL import Image
    from io import BytesIO

    from inference import get_model
    from inference.core.env import WORKFLOWS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STEPS, MAX_ACTIVE_MODELS
    from inference.core.managers.base import ModelManager
    from inference.core.managers.decorators.fixed_size_cache import WithFixedSizeCache
    from inference.core.registries.roboflow import RoboflowModelRegistry
    from inference.core.workflows.core_steps.common.entities import StepExecutionMode
    from inference.core.workflows.execution_engine.core import ExecutionEngine
    from inference.models.utils import ROBOFLOW_MODEL_TYPES

    def build_workflow(model_id: str) -> dict:
        """Build a minimal workflow definition for a given model (detection or classification)."""
        if "classifiers" in model_id or "classification" in model_id:
            step_type = "RoboflowClassificationModel"
        else:
            step_type = "RoboflowObjectDetectionModel"

        return {
            "version": "1.0",
            "inputs": [
                {"type": "WorkflowImage", "name": "image"},
            ],
            "steps": [
                {
                    "type": step_type,
                    "name": "model_step",
                    "image": "$inputs.image",
                    "model_id": model_id,
                }
            ],
            "outputs": [
                {
                    "type": "JsonField",
                    "name": "predictions",
                    "selector": "$steps.model_step.predictions",
                },
            ],
        }

ENT-1355 Split TRT compile into compile, install, and optional register (#2459)

* ENT-1355 Split TRT compile into compile, install, and optional register

Edge devices must keep a local TRT engine when platform upload fails.
Install compiled packages into models-cache and discover them during
negotiation via PlatformRegistrationPolicy.OPTIONAL on edge callers.

* ENT-1355 Address PR review: verify before install, shared TRT constants

Re-raise on REQUIRED registration failures; verify compiled artefacts before
local install. Centralize local TRT manifest constants and slugify via shared
helper; allowlist file handles and use placeholder download URL for discovery.

* Fix KeyPoints construction for supervision 0.29+ API

Use keypoint_confidence when supported, falling back to confidence for
older supervision versions to unblock workflow keypoint visualization tests.

* ENT-1355 Address Pawel review feedback on local TRT discovery

Revert out-of-scope KeyPoints supervision patch. Replace placeholder download
URLs with LocalFileArtefactSpecs and PackageSourceType, teach auto-loader to
resolve local cache packages, return per-variant compilation outcomes, simplify
execute_compilation registration flow, and add weights-provider unit tests.

* ENT-1355 Discover local TRT packages by resolved model id

When a model alias resolves to a different canonical id, local TRT engines
are installed under the resolved cache path. Look up local packages for both
the requested id and resolved id so edge warmup and inference can use them.

* ENT-1355 Address review: untrusted local TRT, md5 verify, load-path fix

- Resolve LOCAL_CACHE packages from the model id they were installed under
 (cache_model_id) so aliased requests load the correct cache directory.
- Make local TRT discovery best-effort: per-package errors are logged and
 skipped, and the discovery call is guarded so a corrupt cache never breaks
 loading of a model with valid platform packages.
- Mark locally compiled packages as untrusted (require allow_untrusted_packages
 to load) and verify md5 (format + content) during discovery.
- Break the roboflow <-> local_trt_packages import cycle by extracting the TRT
 manifest schema (trt_manifest.py) and the cache-path helpers
 (model_cache_paths.py); remove the lazy imports.
- Carry local_install_path through CompilationVariantOutcome and aggregation;
 make CompilationPipelineResult a dataclass; drop the redundant platform_policy
 alias and type _environment_requirements_from_manifest.

* ENT-1355 Cache resolved id for local TRT; avoid double engine hashing

- Persist cache_model_id in the auto-resolution cache so aliased LOCAL_CACHE
 packages rebuild the correct package directory on cache hits instead of
 re-negotiating (and warning) on every load.
- Drop the redundant load-time md5 re-hash of local artefacts; discovery already
 verifies content, so the load path only checks presence and hash format.
- Clarify that local md5 is corruption detection, not tamper protection
 (authenticity is gated by trusted_source=False).

* ENT-1355 Harden local TRT trust gate, install on 409, dedup canonical-first

- Enforce the untrusted-package filter when a package is selected by explicit
 id, so local TRT cannot load without allow_untrusted_packages.
- Under OPTIONAL registration, a post-compile 409 keeps the built engine for
 local install instead of discarding it.
- Discover local packages under the resolved (canonical) id first so a stale
 alias-cache package can't shadow the correct one.
- Re-validate the artefact file handle is a safe basename at the load boundary.
